reconcile.connective: Commentators resolve it by distinguishing two counts: Levi was barred from the general military census but enrolled separately on its own basis for tabernacle service.

discrepancy.connective: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the tension at face value, juxtaposing the command not to number Levi among the children of Israel against the command to number the children of Levi.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Did God tell Moses to number the Levites?"
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Did God tell Moses to number the Levites?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/number-levites.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: That is, along with the other tribes, for it might be numbered by itself, as it afterwards was, Num 3:43 …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill reads the Num 1:49 prohibition as 'not with the other tribes,' and cross-references the separate Levite count in Num 3 — directly dissolving the not-number/number tension.

excerpts.excerpt_text: They were numbered as well as the other tribes; but the enumeration was made on a different principle—for while in the other tribes the number of males was calculated from twenty years and upward [Num 1:3], in that of Levi they were counted "from a month old and upward."
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB states the harmonization outright at the Num 3 command: Levi WAS numbered, only on a different principle (month-old vs twenty-years) than the other tribes' military census.

excerpts.excerpt_text: It was their further honour that as Israel, being a holy people, was not reckoned among the nations, so they, being a holy tribe, were not reckoned among other Israelites, but numbered afterwards by themselves, Num 1:49.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Matthew Henry reconciles both verses: Levi was not reckoned among the other Israelites (Num 1) but numbered afterwards by themselves (Num 3) — a separate, honorary count.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Numbers 1:49
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, reading the Num 1:49 prohibition as 'not along with the other tribes' and pointing to the separate Levite count in Num 3:43; the row's strongest harmonizing anchor (Haley's specific coverage of this pair unconfirmed).

link.note: No allowlisted page squarely resolves the not-numbered/numbered pair: gotquestions.org/Numbers-census.html and defendinginerrancy.com/bible-solutions/Numbers_1.1-4.49.php explain only Levi's exclusion from the military census (or the population-plausibility difficulty) and never address the separate Num 3 count that dissolves the tension. Omitted rather than linked off-topic.
